name: Oholibah
title: Allegorical Representation of Jerusalem
summary: Oholibah is an allegorical name used by the prophet Ezekiel to represent Jerusalem (the kingdom of Judah). In Ezekiel chapter 23, she is portrayed as the sister of Oholah (Samaria), and both are depicted as unfaithful women symbolizing the spiritual adultery and idolatry of Israel and Judah. Oholibah is described as even worse than her sister in her faithlessness toward God.

keyEvents.title: Introduction of the Two Sisters
keyEvents.description: Ezekiel introduces Oholah and Oholibah as two sisters, daughters of the same mother, representing Samaria and Jerusalem respectively. Both engaged in prostitution in Egypt during their youth.

keyEvents.title: Oholibah's Adultery with Assyria
keyEvents.description: Despite having seen her sister Oholah's fate, Oholibah followed in her sin and sought after Assyrian lovers, symbolizing Judah's political and religious alliances with pagan nations.

keyEvents.title: Oholibah's Passionate Pursuit of Babylon
keyEvents.description: Oholibah went even further than her sister, becoming infatuated with Babylonian images and sending messengers to Chaldea, symbolizing Judah's fascination with Babylonian culture and idolatry.

keyEvents.title: God's Abhorrence and Judgment Against Oholibah
keyEvents.description: God turned away from Oholibah just as He had turned away from Oholah. The Lord declares His judgment against her for her faithlessness and moral decay.

keyEvents.title: The Cup of Punishment
keyEvents.description: Oholiba shall drink the same cup as her sister Oholah drank—a cup filled with destruction, sorrow, and ruin, symbolizing Jerusalem's coming fall at Babylon's hand.

keyEvents.title: Final Judgment and Warning
keyEvents.description: God declares final judgment over both sisters for their idolatry, bloodshed, and desecration of the sanctuary. They shall bear the punishment for their sins so that the people of Israel may know that the Lord is God.
